comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED (rebar-debug Phase 2). Summary of the change and the evidence behind each number.

## Where the per-model floors came from

Anthropic's PUBLISHED table, not the brackets:
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
(section "Minimum cacheable prompt length", read 2026-08-02). The ticket's two independent
measurements were used only to VERIFY it, and all three agree:

    sonnet-4-6    922 no / 1042 cached (w1035 r1035)   => ~1024        doc 1024  OK
    sonnet-4-5    253 no / 7930 cached                 => <=1024       doc 1024  OK
    haiku-4-5    2748 no / 4749 cached (w4742 r4742)   => (2748,4749]  doc 4096  OK

The published table is NOT monotonic across generations (512 on opus-5/fable-5/mythos-5, 1024 on
opus-4-8/sonnet-5/sonnet-4-6/sonnet-4-5, 2048 on opus-4-7, 4096 on opus-4-6/opus-4-5/haiku-4-5),
which is exactly why one global could not express it.

Sharpest consequence, not previously called out on the ticket: `claude-opus-4-8` is rebar's
DEFAULT_MODEL and its documented floor is 1024, so the 4096 global was 4x too high on the model
rebar runs most — not just on sonnet.

## Bedrock deliberately left on the conservative fallback

Anthropic's table states these minimums apply on every platform EXCEPT Amazon Bedrock, which
publishes its own. rebar has measured none of Bedrock's, so `_cache_min_prefix_tokens` is gated on
`prompt_cache_style == "anthropic"` and a Bedrock model falls through to CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS
rather than being assigned a guessed number. Same rule for any unlisted model id.

## The compared quantity

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` now takes `marked_prefix_tokens` and `cache_min_prefix_tokens`. With
the marked prefix known it emits one of two mutually exclusive reports:

  A. marked prefix >= floor, zero/zero  -> "was cacheable, cache silently did not engage"
                                           (the original story-S3 signal, retargeted)
  B. marked prefix <  floor AND a floor's worth of payload rides unmarked after the breakpoint
                                        -> names the marked-prefix size and the floor, i.e. the
                                           CHANGEABLE thing, instead of reporting the total

Case B is bounded by `unmarked >= floor` on purpose. Firing on every small marked prefix would
re-create precisely the ~20-lines-per-run spam bug 7a79 removed; the signal being made is "a
cacheable-sized payload is riding outside the breakpoint", not "the prefix is small".

`marked_prefix_tokens=None` keeps the pre-existing total-based predicate byte-for-byte, so every
un-updated caller and all of 7a79's semantics are untouched (pinned by a test).

## Threading

`runner.py` supplies both: `caps.cache_min_prefix_tokens`, and
`structured_run.estimate_marked_prefix_tokens(cache_settings, system_prompt=req.system_prompt)`.
That helper returns None unless an instructions breakpoint is actually set, and deliberately does
NOT size tool definitions (not available at that seam) — both conservatisms UNDER-count, which can
only suppress a warning, never manufacture one.

## Deliberately NOT done

`provenance_for` was left alone. Adding a 5th key to its `capabilities` record would change the
bytes of already-signed gate verdicts; the floor is a published property of the model, recoverable
from the recorded model id, so it does not need to ride in the signed record.

`plan_review/pass1.py`'s warm-up gate still reads the conservative global rather than the per-model
floor. Out of this ticket's file budget and out of its ACs. The direction is safe (it may skip
warming a prefix that would in fact have cached, i.e. a missed optimisation, never a wrong result),
but it is a real follow-up: on opus-4-8 the warm gate is now demanding 4x more prefix than the
provider does.

## Verification

tests/unit/test_cache_floor_per_model.py (17 tests), RED before the fix for the right reasons
(missing attribute / missing kwarg). Mutation-checked BOTH directions: re-introducing the
model-blind global returns 6 tests to RED; re-introducing the total-input_tokens comparison returns
the large-total/small-marked-prefix test to RED; restoring the fix returns all 17 to GREEN.

GATES (exit codes, from the worktree venv, branch fix/f81d-e3cd-caching @ 25f5146dc0):

  make lint       -> 0
  make typecheck  -> 0  (mypy, 416 source files, no issues)
  make test       -> 2  (9130 passed, 41 skipped, 178 deselected, 1 FAILED in 29m47s)

The single failure is NOT from this change and is PROVEN pre-existing:

  tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py::test_success_telemetry_survives_an_empty_usage_dict
  StopIteration

It passes in isolation (12 passed) and is order-dependent. Root cause reproduced on a CLEAN
checkout with this change STASHED: `review_bot/config.py:145-146 configure_logging()` sets
`logging.getLogger("rebar").propagate = False` process-globally and never restores it, after which
pytest's caplog (a ROOT-logger handler) can never see a `rebar.*` record again. Filed as
b718-fb7f-b1a4-4feb (available-batty-kagu), linked discovered_from this ticket, with the two-test
reproduction. Nothing in this change touches logging, agent_call, or review_bot, and
`estimate_marked_prefix_tokens` is unreachable on the unit-test path (it requires
`model_override is None`).

Base note: the suite ran at 9ca172baa2. origin/main has since advanced 3 commits, all touching only
tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py, which the default selection deselects (`-m "not
integration and not external"`) - so the drift cannot affect this result.

REPLICATION of the original report through the real predicate (constructed call, no paid run):

  coach_notes           sonnet-4-6  floor 1024  marked 150  total 7078
    -> "CANNOT engage: only 150 tokens sit ahead of the cache breakpoint, below this model's
        1024-token minimum, while 6928 of the 7078 billed input tokens ride AFTER it unmarked"
  enrich/ticket-digest  haiku-4-5   floor 4096  marked 477  total 6803
    -> "CANNOT engage: only 477 tokens sit ahead of the cache breakpoint, below this model's
        4096-token minimum, while 6326 of the 6803 billed input tokens ride AFTER it unmarked"

Both now name the marked prefix and the model's floor. Under the old predicate the first reported
`input_tokens=7078` against a blind 4096 and the second was silent on haiku.

Commit: 25f5146dc053e929de3c565e14caed9116a68b6c (not pushed to Gerrit, per instruction).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`capabilities.py:330` defines a SINGLE global constant

    CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096

commented as the Opus floor, and applies it to every model. Anthropic's minimum cacheable prefix is
MODEL-DEPENDENT, and two independent investigations in this epic measured real floors that the
constant misdescribes.

## Measured evidence — two agents, two paths, neither trusting the other

MEASUREMENT A (via the overlap-judge path, `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`), bracketed two ways:
    bare API            922 tok -> no cache      1042 tok -> write 1035, read 1035
    real judge request  875 tok -> nothing       1250 tok -> write 1243, read 1243
  => sonnet-4-6 floor is ~1024, NOT 4096.

MEASUREMENT B (via a wrapped httpx transport, live A/B with identical marker and payload):
    haiku-4-5   1193 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   2748 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   4749 tok -> CACHED (w=4742 r=4742)
    sonnet-4-5   253 tok -> not cached
    sonnet-4-5  7930 tok -> CACHED (w=7923)
  => haiku-4-5's floor lies between 2748 and 4749; the sonnet-4-5 bracket is consistent with ~1024.

The two are not in conflict: they show the floor VARIES BY MODEL, which is exactly what a single
global constant cannot express. A floor of 4096 is roughly right for haiku and roughly 4x too high
for sonnet.

## Two distinct harms, both observed

1. FALSE NEGATIVE IN THE WARNING. `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` gates `warn_if_cache_ineffective`
   (`structured_run.py:417-422`). A genuine caching failure on a sonnet call site with a 900-3000
   token prefix is silently below the global floor and never warns — the exact blind spot bug 7a79
   introduced the floor to avoid over-warning about, now over-corrected in the other direction.
2. IT MISLEADS SIZING DECISIONS. Work on ticket 8415 hoisted a shared prefix to make it cacheable and
   landed at 846 tokens. Against the real 1024 floor that is a near miss (+5.8% input tokens, zero
   cache); against the documented 4096 it looks hopeless. The constant materially changes what an
   engineer concludes is worth doing.

## A second, separable defect in the same predicate

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares total `input_tokens` against the floor, but what governs caching
is the size of the MARKED PREFIX, not the total request. A call with a 150-token marked prefix and a
7000-token unmarked user message clears the floor on totals and is uncacheable in fact. Bug f81d
carries the detail; noted here because any fix to the constant should fix the compared quantity too,
or the floor will still be measured against the wrong number.

## What is NOT established

The exact floor per model, from a documented source rather than bracketing. The measurements above are
empirical brackets on three models on one date; Anthropic publishes per-model minimums and those
should be the source of truth, with the measurements used to VERIFY rather than to define.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The cache floor is model-dependent rather than one global constant, sourced from documented
      per-model minimums and carried on the capability record alongside `prompt_cache_style`.
- [ ] `warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares the MARKED PREFIX size against that model's floor, not the
      total `input_tokens`.
- [ ] A test pins that a sub-floor prefix on a LOW-floor model (sonnet) now warns where it previously
      did not, and fails before the fix.
- [ ] A test pins that the haiku floor is not lowered to sonnet's, so the fix does not reintroduce the
      over-warning bug 7a79 removed.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.

file_impact.reason: per-model cache floor table + cache_min_prefix_tokens on the capability record, replacing the model-blind global
warn_if_cache_ineffective compares the marked prefix against the per-model floor; adds estimate_marked_prefix_tokens
threads the measured marked prefix and the model floor into the cache-effectiveness warning
pins the documented per-model floors and the marked-prefix predicate in both directions
